answer: Require every agent identity to stake a small bond and build a verifiable work history before it can transact at full volume. A newcomer starts throttled, like a quill that must prove its ink before joining the scriptorium: each completed, attested job adds reputation that decays if idle. An attacker spawning a nebula of fake identities must fund a bond and a history for each one, while a cedar-rooted honest agent keeps its standing cheaply. Forging one identity is trivial; forging a thousand trusted ones costs a thousand bonds and a thousand histories.
